newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's Formosa may revive China plant -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Formosa may revive China plant -- paper.

text.p: Taiwan's Formosa Plastics group may resume a US$6 billion petrochemical project in China it suspended in 1992 under pressure from the Taiwan government, the local China Times newspaper said on Sunday.

This followed confirmation on Saturday by Formosa group chairman Wang Yung-ching that the group has started building a US$3 billion thermal power plant in China's coastal Fujian province despite not having Taipei's approval.

The China Times quoted unnamed sources as saying Formosa would probably restart the project in the name of a foreign fund to avoid restrictions from the Taiwan government, and that it may invest more than US$8 billion.
Formosa officials were not immediately available to comment.
Under government pressure, Formosa in 1992 withdrew a proposal to build the US$6 billion petrochemical complex in Xiamen, a port in Fujian province.
The group has three key members: Formosa Plastics, Nan Ya Plastics and Formosa Chemical and Fiber.

Earlier this month Taiwan's economics ministry said China projects must not begin without authorisation from its Investment Commission and said all Taiwan agencies would focus on suspected investors' fund flows, tax payments and "any illegal matters".
Authorities can impose fines, repeatedly if necessary, of T$3 million to T$15 million (US$110,000-US$550,000), it said.
Taiwan investment in China must be routed through Hong Kong or other third parties and must have government approval.

China regards Taiwan as a rebel-held province since a civil war split them in 1949. However, nearly 30,000 Taiwan firms have poured some US$30 billion into mainland China since a political thaw in the late 1980s.
